listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Monday, October 26. Our lead story is from Brazil. President Lula has been elected to a fourth term. The 80-year-old left-wing leader defeated Flávio Bolsonaro in a bitterly contested runoff. Reports describe the vote as narrow. Flávio Bolsonaro is a Trump ally and the son of the former Brazilian president. Brazil is Latin America's largest economy and its biggest democracy. NPR had said U.S. influence in the region was at stake in the race. Now the front page. In Serbia, President Vučić says it is clear his party has lost an election. The vote was billed as a referendum on the country's future. A student-led protest movement came out ahead, and there were celebrations. In tech, Anthropic is launching an expanded Cyber Verification Program. It gives qualifying security professionals advanced cyber capabilities, with fewer blocking classifiers. In politics, Attorney General Todd Blanche defended a Justice Department lawsuit over Alaska's Senate race. The suit would block the results if the Republican loses. He spoke on CNN. Now a quick look at each section. In tech, a new design skill called hallmark aims to keep AI-built interfaces from looking generic. Also, Kimi K3.1 Pro is live on the Kimi API, with open weights promised by November fourth. In politics, NPR asks whether polls showing a Democratic sweep can be trusted. The picture is more complicated in the closest House races. In world news, Russia says it will open a humanitarian corridor to the occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky. Uganda is imposing a 21-day quarantine on citizens returning from DR Congo. And China's four-day Party Plenum begins today in Beijing. In sports, the Rockets are three and oh and face the Hawks. ESPN reports the 49ers lost to the Falcons in Week 7 and now head into their bye week. Also, Olson has won his sixth Fielding Bible Award. In Atlanta, a letter to the editor weighs in on the proposed three and a half billion dollar Beltline rail project. The city's first bike park, on the Westside, is nearly finished. In architecture, AEC Magazine says the next bottleneck for AI may be checking engineering work. ArchDaily looks at material choices for new floors added to historic buildings. In science, today's NASA picture of the day shows the Great Nebula in Orion. NASA's Swift Observatory has ended its science mission. And a study in Nature links Australia's wildfire vulnerability to the colonial disruption of Indigenous fire management. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Brazil's left-wing President Lula elected for fourth term
lead.note: Brazil's President Lula has been elected to a fourth term. The 80-year-old left-wing leader defeated Flávio Bolsonaro in a bitterly contested runoff. Reports describe the vote as narrow and knife-edge. The race was between Lula's legacy and Flávio Bolsonaro, a Trump ally and the son of the former Brazilian president. Brazil is Latin America's largest economy and its biggest democracy, and NPR had framed the runoff as one in which U.S. influence in the region was at stake. For the reader, this is a major election result in the news today, and it reaches beyond Brazil's borders. The result settles who will lead the country, while the margin and the bitter tone of the campaign are both part of the story. Further coverage looks at how Lula turned the race around.
